clue.text: Form of escort public or private?

indicators.note: to form something from material is to shape it anew, so the word that follows is remade

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether an escort agency belongs to the state or is privately run.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of ESCORT gives SECTOR, and the economy has a public sector and a private one.
explanation.definitionFit: Economists divide an economy into parts called the public sector and the private sector.

clue.text: Poet inclined to blue?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Stephen ..., the English poet
second meaning: one who tends to blow money freely, blue being slang for squander

explanation.walkthrough: Blue here is a variant of blow, to squander money, not the colour or a mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephen Spender was a twentieth-century poet, and a big spender is someone who splashes cash freely.

clue.text: Fashionable old poet with unknown brother of comedy

parts.note: Omar Khayyam, the Persian poet of the Rubaiyat

explanation.surface: A stylish old poet teams up with an unknown comedy sibling.
explanation.walkthrough: Omar Khayyam is the old poet, not Homer or Virgil; the pieces run across the word break.
explanation.definitionFit: Chico was one of the Marx Brothers, the American family comedy team.

clue.text: Work with model on the other side

definitions.note: the answer is a noun, someone who is on the other side

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
a poser is one who poses, like a model

explanation.surface: A piece of work done with a model who has switched sides.
explanation.definitionFit: An opposer argues against a motion, standing in the opposing camp.

clue.text: Wise man in old city, an old religious disputant

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it is placed inside it

parts.note: Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city
a sage is a wise man

explanation.surface: A sage living in an ancient city argues about religion.
explanation.walkthrough: The Usagers were eighteenth-century Nonjurors who argued for restoring certain old communion usages, which is why the clue calls them old.
explanation.definitionFit: The Usagers were an eighteenth-century faction of Nonjuring clergy who quarrelled over communion rites.

clue.text: Wait under a second with the eyes of an optimist

definitions.text: with the eyes of an optimist

indicators.note: in a down clue, being under means coming lower, so later in the reading order

parts.note: s is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: Someone waiting just a moment, looking hopeful.
explanation.walkthrough: Starry-eyed means naively hopeful, so starry is the idealist's kind of eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: Being starry-eyed means idealistically hopeful, the outlook of an unrealistic optimist.

clue.text: Sprouting from 10 margin, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters could be arranged in some other way

parts.note: the number written as a word

explanation.surface: Something growing out of the margin of clue 10.
explanation.walkthrough: The 10 looks like a cross-reference to 10 across; it is just the number ten.
explanation.definitionFit: A germinant seed is one that is germinating, putting out shoots and beginning to grow.

clue.text: Pink eggs round the throne

indicators.note: being round something means surrounding it on both sides

explanation.surface: Pink-coloured eggs laid around a throne.
explanation.walkthrough: Fish eggs are roe, and the throne is simply a seat.
explanation.definitionFit: Roseate means rose-coloured, a rosy pink shade.

clue.text: Poet's round against poet, a juicy addition

indicators.note: the possessive with round means this one surrounds what follows

parts.note: Thomas Gray, author of the Elegy in a Country Churchyard

explanation.surface: One poet squares up against another, with something juicy thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: GRAY goes round V, and Browning follows. Gravy browning is a colouring added to darken gravy and meat juices.
explanation.definitionFit: The colouring product is stirred into meat gravy, an extra ingredient for the juices.

clue.text: Primo and Nahum, the poet, get a lift

explanation.surface: Two literary men with unusual first names hitch a ride somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Each first name stands for its surname: Primo Levi and Nahum Tate.
explanation.definitionFit: To levitate is to rise into the air, which is a jokey way of being raised up.

clue.text: By obtaining a degree, Robert, the poet, goes where it's always cold

parts.note: per means by, as in per post

explanation.surface: Robert Frost, freshly graduated, heads off to somewhere freezing.
explanation.definitionFit: Permafrost is ground that stays frozen throughout the year, so the place is permanently icy.

clue.text: Poem doesn't end on notes that are nasty

indicators.note: a word that does not reach its end has its final letter cut off

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: An unfinished poem written on nasty notes.
explanation.walkthrough: ODE loses its last letter to give OD; IOUs are written notes of debt.
explanation.definitionFit: Something odious is hateful or repulsive, a stronger synonym for unpleasant.

clue.text: Maidenly old poet goes round North America

indicators.note: going round something means encircling it, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: Virgil, the Roman poet of the Aeneid

explanation.surface: A demure ancient poet tours North America.
explanation.definitionFit: Virginal describes someone chaste and pure, like a maiden who has kept her innocence.

clue.text: Ban writer earning money?

parts.note: a pro is a professional, paid for the work
a scribe is one who writes

explanation.surface: A paid professional author is suddenly barred.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces go in reverse clue order: a writer earning money is a pro scribe.
explanation.definitionFit: To proscribe something is to forbid or outlaw it officially.

clue.text: Conceit which poet has to face?

definitions.text: Conceit which poet has to face?

parts.note: side is swagger, putting on airs

explanation.surface: A vain poet must confront his own arrogance.
explanation.walkthrough: Conceit looks like a poetic figure of speech; here it is vanity. The whole clue also hints at the whiskers grown down the face.
explanation.definitionFit: Sideburns are strips of whiskers grown down the cheeks beside the ears.

clue.text: See 9
Lots of paper put on before going in

definitions.meaning: first meaning: blocks of writing sheets
second meaning: leg guards a cricketer straps on before going in to bat

explanation.surface: Instructions about preparing piles of paper.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman goes in to bat, wearing protective leg guards called pads.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing tablets of stacked sheets are pads, and so are the padded leg guards worn by batsmen.

clue.text: Supply lions with some eggs to eat

indicators.note: eating something takes it inside, so one piece swallows the other

parts.note: a pride is a group of lions
some of the word ova, eggs

explanation.surface: Feeding a pride of lions with a few eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: Ova is the Latin plural for eggs, and only part of it is used.
explanation.definitionFit: To provide is to supply or furnish something needed.

clue.text: Dot's follower, a modern poet, causes a stir

parts.note: in a web address, com follows the dot

explanation.surface: Someone who follows Dot, along with a contemporary poet, creates a fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: Dot looks like a woman's name; it is the dot in dot-com.
explanation.definitionFit: A commotion is a noisy disturbance, the same as a stir or fuss.

clue.text: China semi-involved with Japanese finance?

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the word is mixed into a fresh order

parts.note: the sen is a Japanese monetary unit, a hundredth of a yen

explanation.surface: China is partly caught up with Japanese money matters.
explanation.walkthrough: China looks like the country; it is porcelain. Meissen in Germany made Europe's first hard-paste porcelain.
explanation.definitionFit: Meissen is fine porcelain made in the Saxon town of that name, so it is a kind of china.

clue.text: Broken idol, curious container for fuel

indicators.note: something broken is smashed into pieces that can be put back differently

parts.note: rum means strange in British slang

explanation.surface: A smashed idol and an odd fuel can.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil drum is a large cylindrical barrel used for holding petroleum.

clue.text: Jinx on poet with rings

parts.note: two rings look like two Os

explanation.surface: A curse falls on a poet wearing rings.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoodoo is a bringer of bad luck, much like a curse.

clue.text: Give name with nothing in it to fool with old gold coin

indicators.note: having something in it means a word holds another inside

parts.note: to dub is to give a name
a loon is a crazy fool

explanation.surface: Naming a fool after nothing, with an antique coin involved.
explanation.definitionFit: The doubloon was a Spanish gold coin, famous from pirate stories.

clue.text: Smoke seriously in hospital and drink

parts.note: H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A patient smokes heavily in hospital and has a drink too.
explanation.definitionFit: A serious smoker draws the smoke down into the lungs rather than just puffing.

clue.text: Poet to take one back?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Greek epic poet of the Iliad
second meaning: a homing pigeon, which carries you back home

explanation.walkthrough: A homer is a homing pigeon; the clue's second half is a playful description of something that returns home.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek bard wrote the Odyssey, and a homing pigeon flies back to its loft.

clue.text: Fool gets all Yorkshire to make hard cases

parts.note: Yorkshire was historically divided into three Ridings, North, East and West

explanation.surface: An idiot takes over the whole of Yorkshire to toughen up some tough characters.
explanation.walkthrough: Nitriding is a metallurgical process that forms a hard nitrogen-rich case on steel; the plural is its products.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitriding hardens a metal's surface layer, so nitridings are hardened surface casings on steel.

clue.text: See 2
From which to take us to Nuneaton?

definitions.text: From which to take us to Nuneaton?

indicators.note: taking letters from a run of words means lifting them out of it

explanation.surface: A traveller asks where to catch a train to Nuneaton.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits across tak-E US TO N-uneaton. Euston is the London terminus for trains up the West Coast line through Nuneaton, a Warwickshire town.
explanation.definitionFit: Trains from the London rail terminus run north through the Warwickshire town on the West Coast main line.

clue.text: Social worker for border county

parts.note: ants are social insects, and the workers are ants

explanation.surface: A social worker is posted to a county on the frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: Social worker suggests a welfare officer; here it is a worker ant. Antrim is a county of Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Antrim is one of the six historic counties in Northern Ireland.
